scope: Read-only local source/artifact inspection and official documentation; no source mutation, Cargo, Windows, CI or Git mutation. Win7 CI status not inspected or inferred.
confirmed: Three local extern system declarations use link(name=ole32) and link_name=CoTaskMemFree. Renaming the Rust item does not rename that external symbol.

windows 0.62.2 generated Win32::System::Com::CoTaskMemFree declares combase.dll via windows_core::link!. windows-core 0.62.2 imp/bindings.rs independently declares the same name via windows_link; Array::clear uses it. That generic source existence alone does not prove Array is instantiated by this application.

windows-link 0.2.1 on x86 emits raw-dylib,+verbatim,import_name_type=undecorated. Rust documents raw-dylib as generating an import library; plain dylib instead searches an existing import library. The local declarations and generated imports expose the same native symbol.

The actual Modern product import table retains combase.dll!CoTaskMemFree; therefore the three plain Ole32 library annotations did not achieve the required final import boundary. The result does not identify the sole contributing import-library member or call site.

Captured SDK provenance is VS17.14.37824.6, MSVC tools14.44.35207/linker14.44.35229.0, SDK10.0.26100.0. The report captures cl/linker/staticCRT/kernel32.lib hashes but not ole32.lib bytes, linker /VERBOSE selection or link map. It cannot prove a specific SDK Ole32 forwarding member as unique cause.

officialPrimary.supports: Documented default OLE allocator, void return/null no-op, Ole32.lib/Ole32.dll, minimum Windows2000. These requirements support the Win7 API contract, not actual Win7 execution certification.
Resolve exact exported name from specified module; NULL failure; match case/spelling; resolve by name instead of ordinal. No arbitrary module selection is needed.
Already-loaded module only. Full path avoids ambiguous duplicate basenames. Default increments reference count; PIN holds until process exit; UNCHANGED_REFCOUNT can race unload. XP minimum.
System directory path with explicit bounded buffer; zero failure, required-size/truncation handling. No hardcoded Windows drive or environment-supplied DLL directory.
Read actual loaded module path with bounded truncation checks; returned path spelling/short-name form may differ. Must fail safely rather than truncate or silently accept arbitrary basename.
Decrements reference count; BOOL failure/GetLastError; do not release an unincremented GetModuleHandle reference.
dylib versus raw-dylib import-library behavior, and extern system is stdcall on Windows x86_32. Function pointer ABI must exactly match one pointer argument and void return.

recommendedCandidate.shape: Private shared task allocator capability with exact unsafe extern system fn(*const c_void) function pointer; all three adapters acquire it before any API that can transfer task memory.
recommendedCandidate.module: Construct fixed Ole32.dll full system path with bounded GetSystemDirectoryW; GetModuleHandleExW against that full path, since Ole32 already has static COM imports. No LoadLibrary basename, DLL search-policy changes, or environment lookup. Optional bounded GetModuleFileNameW identity validation must handle truncation and WOW64/path representation conservatively.
recommendedCandidate.lifetime: Hold an incremented module reference until every task pointer obtained in that operation is freed, and check actual FreeLibrary outcome; if a single process-lifetime PIN is chosen instead, make the intentional permanent system-module pin explicit and bounded rather than accumulating references per call. No pointer may outlive its module capability.
recommendedCandidate.resolve: GetProcAddress(module, exact ASCII CoTaskMemFree + NUL); fail before allocation if missing. Transmute only non-null FARPROC to exact extern system ABI, retain the capability, call once per transferred allocation including conversion errors. No call to generated windows CoTaskMemFree or static extern of that symbol.
recommendedCandidate.forwarding: Do not infer Ole32 identity from an imported CoInitializeEx function address: it may resolve to a forwarded implementation. Exact Ole32 export resolution may legitimately forward on modern Windows; this is distinct from a static combase dependency in our EXE.
recommendedCandidate.otherAllocations: Do not alter LocalFree/BSTR/CRT allocator families or use Rust allocator/HeapFree for task storage. No DLL handle/fn pointer enters domain/protocol.
recommendedCandidate.failure: Resolver failure aborts the operation before task allocation. Resource-release errors need exact ownership/fault handling, never silently treat a dropped Rust wrapper as physical module release.

necessaryProofAfterAuthorizedImplementat: Both actual Modern and Win7 MSVC final EXE and relevant tests: inspect raw PE imports; no combase.dll CoTaskMemFree and no new winrt-error/API-set import regression. GNU success alone is insufficient.
Capture chosen SDK import-library provenance/link map if attributing original unique cause; not needed to avoid static task allocator symbol via explicit runtime resolution.
Meaningful resolver missing/invalid-module-before-allocation tests and cleanup on task-string conversion failure; x86 ABI and one-free ownership assertions.
Real authorized Win11 query/picker use only in owned hidden fixture where applicable; Win7/10/Seewo remain separate actual runtime gates.
limitations: No proof of exclusive original linker root cause without link-map/import-library evidence.
Modern CI success is not Win7 loader/runtime compatibility. Win7 ongoing CI conclusion is deliberately absent.
No production fix or new test execution in this research.
